## Example 2.2(a) · Model the tide {#fgt2-tide-model .trig-lesson .application-lesson}

The tide at a point on the NSW coast can be modelled using the equation $h=a\cos(nt)+b$. At Fort Denison over two consecutive days, high tide is 1.8 m and low tide is 0.6 m. The time between high tide and low tide is 8 hours. Let $t$ be the number of hours since high tide.

**a)** Determine the values of $a$, $n$, and $b$ which model the tide at Fort Denison.

::: {.takeaway}
**Hint:** What are the [amplitude]{.parameter-a}, [period]{.parameter-n} and [midline]{.parameter-k}?
:::

<p class="booklet-cue">Booklet p. 29 · Example 2.2(a)</p>

::: notes

Work in OneNote. The time origin is high tide, so positive cosine is a convenient model. a=0.6, b=1.2 and T=16 hours; n=2π/16=π/8 radians per hour. Hence h=0.6 cos(πt/8)+1.2. Explain the role of the booklet's b as the midline parameter k in our general sketching form. Height is measured in metres and time in hours. The slide gives a static hint to identify the amplitude, period and midline; complete the model in OneNote. There are no answer-reveal controls on this slide. Allow about 5 minutes.

:::
